content.value_statement: RAG projects fail when retrieval quality, source controls, and evaluation are designed too late. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through vector stores, chunking, retrieval, reranking, citations, and tests.
actual_capabilities: Compares vector store options such as Pinecone, Weaviate, Milvus, Chroma, Qdrant, and FAISS.
Explains dense, sparse, hybrid, multi-query, and HyDE retrieval strategies.
Shows chunking approaches for recursive text, tokens, semantic boundaries, and Markdown headers.
Covers reranking with cross-encoders, MMR, and LLM-based scoring.
Provides prompt patterns for context-only answers, citations, and confidence reporting.
Lists evaluation signals for accuracy, retrieval quality, and groundedness.
limitations: It is guidance, not a complete runnable RAG application.
It does not include the referenced assets or deeper reference files in this package.
Provider setup, authentication, data governance, and deployment remain user responsibilities.
Example snippets may need adaptation for each library version and runtime.

use_cases.title: Prototype a document Q&A assistant
use_cases.description: Developers can plan a chatbot that retrieves product, support, or policy documents before answering user questions.

use_cases.title: Improve enterprise knowledge search
use_cases.description: Data engineers can compare storage, metadata, update cadence, and retrieval methods for internal documents.

use_cases.title: Evaluate grounded AI answers
use_cases.description: Product teams can design test questions, groundedness checks, and citation behavior before launch.

prompt_templates.title: Map My First RAG Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the RAG implementation skill to design a basic document Q&A system for [corpus]. Include corpus scope, chunking, embeddings, vector store, retrieval flow, and success checks.

prompt_templates.title: Choose Retrieval Strategy
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare dense, sparse, hybrid, and multi-query retrieval for [use case]. Recommend one approach with tradeoffs, metadata filters, reranking needs, and evaluation metrics.

prompt_templates.title: Design Production Pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a production RAG pipeline for [domain]. Include ingestion, access control, incremental updates, chunking, embeddings, vector store configuration, retrieval, reranking, citations, monitoring, and rollback.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose Retrieval Quality
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this RAG failure: [symptom]. Build a troubleshooting plan for chunk size, embeddings, query reformulation, metadata filters, reranking, prompt grounding, and test cases.

output_examples.input: Build a support documentation Q&A assistant.
output_examples.output: A concise architecture plan covering document ingestion, chunk sizing, vector store choice, hybrid retrieval, citations, and groundedness checks.

output_examples.input: Retrieval returns irrelevant answers for policy questions.
output_examples.output: A troubleshooting checklist for metadata filters, query variants, reranking, chunk overlap, missing documents, and answer prompts.

output_examples.input: Compare vector stores for an internal knowledge base.
output_examples.output: A decision summary comparing managed, open-source, local, and high-performance stores by scale, operations, filtering, and deployment model.

best_practices: Define access rules before indexing documents, especially for restricted or customer data.
Evaluate retrieval and answer quality with test questions before production use.
Return citations and source metadata when responses depend on retrieved content.
anti_patterns: Indexing documents before defining chunking rules, metadata, and refresh cadence.
Using a single retrieval method without testing sparse, dense, or hybrid search.
Treating high similarity scores as proof that an answer is grounded.

faq.question: Does this skill build a full RAG app?
faq.answer: No. It gives implementation guidance, patterns, and examples that an agent can adapt to your stack.

faq.question: Which vector database should I choose?
faq.answer: Choose based on scale, filtering, operations, and deployment needs. The skill compares Pinecone, Weaviate, Milvus, Chroma, Qdrant, and FAISS.

faq.question: Can it help reduce hallucinations?
faq.answer: Yes. It focuses on retrieval, citations, and prompts that require answers to use supplied context.

faq.question: Does it include security guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. It warns users to redact sensitive data, enforce access controls, and avoid exposing restricted source documents.

faq.question: Can Claude Code or Codex use it?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill is written for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: What data do I need before using it?
faq.answer: Prepare representative documents, target questions, access rules, freshness requirements, and expected answer examples.
